summary: Eldorado NF lookout built 1931 by the state and forest service; removed 2007-08 and given to Placerville; pieces reported at Gold Bug Park; no rebuild found.

facts.design: 80-foot tower with 7x7 foot cab; NHLR calls it a Pacific Coast Steel tower, FFLOS an X-Brace tower
facts.status_note: Taken apart at the peak in 2007-08; a Mountain Democrat article says the pieces were being stored at Gold Bug Park, Placerville; no source describes the peak site today
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service; built as a joint station with the State Division of Forestry

events.note: Completed in 1931; the Mountain Democrat reported the 80-foot tower finished the week of July 3, 1931
Joint station; Forest Service lookout Carlos Tidwell and state lookout Tevis Mitchell alternated duty
Annual fire guard training school held at the lookout
Annual school of instruction for fire guards and rangers opened at the Baltic Peak lookout
Sly Park brush fire of over a quarter acre, spotted from the lookout by Mrs. Eula Mae Nevins
City sale notice says the tower stayed in operation until approximately 1996
Registered May 29, 2003 as US 514, CA 52; nominated by Mark Swift
Plans finalized to move the tower from the peak to the County Fairgrounds at Placerville; the city later delivered it to Gold Bug Park instead
Removed in 2007-08 and donated to the City of Placerville for potential restoration
Delivered to Gold Bug Park, Placerville, in 2008; NHLR says moved in four sections
City of Placerville sale notice; sealed bids due February 23, 2017, to a buyer who would rebuild the tower within El Dorado County
Registered December 21, 2019 as US 1868, CA 63; nominated by Brad Eells

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR describes an 80-foot Pacific Coast Steel tower similar to an LS-40 Aermotor, while FFLOS says an X-Brace tower. The story reports both descriptions and does not choose one.
NHLR gives 5,046 ft (1,538 m) and FFLOS gives 5,084 ft (1,550 m). The brief keeps the NHLR figure, and the story gives no elevation.
A 2005 account planned a move to the County Fairgrounds, but the city's later account says the tower was delivered to Gold Bug Park in 2008 and the fairgrounds did not want to pay for the base.

notes_for_editor: The Mountain Democrat article shows no year; it says the tower was gifted '10 years ago' and gives a Thursday, Feb. 23 proposal deadline, which matches the 2017 sale notice, so it is probably from February 2017. The story calls it an undated Mountain Democrat article. No source read gives the outcome of the February 2017 sale; the City resolution declaring the tower surplus (evogov 40043.pdf) appeared only in search snippets and was not read. The brief's elevation is kept from NHLR, and FFLOS gives a different figure. The brief record is consistent with 80 ft (24.4 m). Access is left out because no source read gives access to the peak or to Gold Bug Park. Two WebSearch calls and five distinct page reads were used; the Mountain Democrat homepage fetch returned HTTP 429 and a later attempt at the old URL returned 404.
